items.message: The `ref` parameter is passed unsanitized directly into a `git show` argument formatted as `{ref}:{path}`. An attacker who controls `ref` (e.g. via a crafted call passing `ref="HEAD --upload-pack=malicious"` or a ref name containing shell metacharacters) could manipulate the subprocess invocation. File contents read from git at an arbitrary ref are decoded with `errors='replace'`, which means binary or non-UTF-8 file contents are silently mangled before being stored in a `FileChange`. If those mangled bytes are later written back into a worktree and executed as test code or source, the round-trip is lossy and the materialized file will not match the committed file.
